findings.summary: Promise identity activation uses the shared default-library provenance classifier.
Runtime delete key selection reuses its literal-union proof without a redundant filter.
Owned JSON assignment and rest copy ordered entries directly; native getter views retain key snapshots and presence checks.
Identity comparison observations reuse validated operand types without repeated checker queries or union walks.
Length-property provenance uses the shared named symbol reader.
Reached Promise observations reuse the program index; obsolete producer scans and unused context dependencies are removed.
Promise consumer checks iterate the existing Set without allocating an array per expression.
Iterator result absence uses the existing null-only slot proof and one owned-present Nullable factory.
Await and async return adoption share the existing wrapper traversal and one contextual-storage boundary.
Property-assignment receiver retention uses the existing snapshot_value helper to state its intentional owning copy or move.
